author: Macarius the Egyptian
occasion: The homilies exhort Christians to pursue the indwelling of the Holy Spirit now, so that the hidden glory of the soul may be revealed in the body at the resurrection.
argument: Christians differ wholly from people of this world: the latter are bound to earthly things, while Christians long for the love of the heavenly Father, Him alone before their eyes with much desire. The world of Christians is another, and their conduct, mind, word, and action is other. Believers must strive through faith and virtuous living to acquire now the heavenly garment, because whatever glory the soul stores within will be revealed outwardly in the body on the day of resurrection. The author uses the image of spring, when trees, after winter has passed, warmed by invisible power from the sun and winds, put forth leaves like garments, flowers, and fruits, and the flowers of the grass come forth from within the bosom of the earth, as a type of the resurrection. For true Christians, the resurrection day is like the first month, Xanthicus, called April, when the glory of the Holy Spirit, hidden in their souls, will come forth and clothe their bodies. That Spirit will then be to them garment, food, drink, exultation, joy, peace, vine, and eternal life.

outline.move: The homily contrasts Christians with people of this world, showing that Christians have another world, and other conduct, mind, word, and action, and that they long for the love of the heavenly Father.

The homily urges believers to acquire the heavenly garment now through faith and virtue, and explains that the hidden glory of the Spirit will be revealed in their bodies at the resurrection, using spring as an image.

cast.name: Solomon
cast.who: Biblical king cited from the Gospels as an example of earthly glory that cannot match the lilies.

cast.name: the Lord
cast.who: Jesus Christ, quoted as saying that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of the lilies.

voices.speaker: the Lord (quoted saying)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by 'περὶ ὧν ὁ Κύριος εἶπεν' and given as direct speech.

key_terms.sense: True Christians, those who possess the Spirit and long for the heavenly Father, as opposed to people of the world.
The present world and its earthly attachments, from which Christians are separated.
The heavenly garment or clothing of glory that the soul acquires now and that will cover the body at the resurrection.
The glory of the Holy Spirit hidden in the soul now and revealed outwardly in the body at the resurrection.
The Holy Spirit, whose indwelling power and glory will be manifested in believers' bodies.
The resurrection day, when the bodies of the saints will be glorified.
The first month in the Macedonian calendar, identified in the text as the month called April, used as an image of the resurrection season.
The sun of righteousness, a title for Christ whose power brings forth the hidden glory in believers.
The soul, the inward person where the Spirit's glory is stored and hidden until the resurrection.
The body, which will be clothed and glorified by the hidden glory of the soul at the resurrection.

scripture: The author quotes the saying about Solomon and the lilies, which appears in Matthew 6:29 and Luke 12:27. He refers to the Lord's saying without a formal citation. Psalm numbering and Old Testament book names are not used in these sections.
uncertain: The exact date of composition of the Spiritual Homilies.
Whether the homilies were originally delivered orally and later collected.
The precise identity of the addressee or original audience beyond a general Christian readership.
The identity of the speaker in sections 5-6; the name Macarius does not appear in the source text provided.
